findings.reason: Verified that the migration indexes `[0]['id']` on a join result that is empty whenever `embed_category` is unset (the default is not stored in `site_settings`); `PG::Result#[]` then raises IndexError before the fallback can run, so the migration aborts.

The old setting and its specs accepted values like `http://` and `https://example.com/1234`, and the migration inserts each line raw (also interpolated into SQL); `record_for_host` compares against the bare `uri.host`, so those migrated rows silently stop matching.

The format regex accepts a `:port` and `before_validation` strips only the scheme and path, while `record_for_host` compares against `uri.host`, which has no port; so a host saved with a port can never match, and the `{2,5}` TLD limit really does reject longer TLDs.

After save the client sets the category with `findById(this.get('categoryId'))`, which is undefined when no category was chosen, even though the server stored Uncategorized; this is a minor display glitch until reload.
Correct that `destroyRecord()` has no `.catch`, unlike `save`; this is a minor UX gap.
Correct that an unknown id or a nil host raises NoMethodError and returns a 500 instead of a 404/422, but only on admin-only endpoints and with unusual input.
There is indeed no uniqueness constraint and `.first` has no order, but duplicate hosts with different categories need an unusual admin action.
Correct that `expandable_first_post?` no longer checks hosts, so the example name and the fabrication in `before` are misleading; this is test naming and cleanup.
Verified that the contents of the two fabricator files are swapped; Fabrication loads all files so it still works, and this is file-organization cleanup.
Verified that the pretender `/fruits/:id` always returns `fruits[0]`, so `find('fruit', 2)` with apple's colors is misleading; this is a minor test-correctness issue.
Correct that `map` throws on null `*_ids`, leaves undefined entries for ids missing from the root, and makes `|| []` dead code; but no current payload sends null.
Correct that `String#replace` with a string pattern replaces only the first underscore, but no current model is affected.
Verified that `update` is a no-op and that no template references `saveChanges`; this is dead-code cleanup.
